claims.text: The proposed Mg-transition-metal alloy is lightweight, with density below 6 g/cm³.
Mechanically alloyed or pre-alloyed Mg-transition-metal powder with particle size below 45 µm is an appropriate initial state.
The initial powder contains residual oxides and may retain segregation introduced during milling.
SPS at 925 °C for 10 minutes, 100 °C/min, and 50 MPa in vacuum or argon will provide the desired processing condition.
An intermediate sintering temperature of 925 °C ±25 °C will maximize relative density above 98%.
Processing near 925 °C will minimize brittle Mg-Zn-rich or Mg-Al-rich intermetallic phases.
Mg volatilization becomes significant above 950 °C under vacuum or low pressure.
Rapid SPS heating and short dwell time allow densification before substantial segregation or volatilization occurs.
Rapid heating bypasses an instability window and produces a metastable single-phase-like solid solution or fine-grained eutectic structure.
High uniaxial pressure promotes particle rearrangement and neck growth at lower temperatures than conventional sintering.
Keeping the temperature below the proposed threshold avoids the nucleation and growth of brittle Laves phases or oxides.
Short exposure and a protective atmosphere minimize Mg volatility.
Relative density falls below 95% when the sintering temperature is below 850 °C because diffusion is insufficient.
Temperatures above 975 °C or dwell times above 15 minutes cause more than 5% Mg loss, resulting in porosity and microstructural instability.
The optimized material will have relative density above 98.5%.
The optimized material will have grain size below 5 µm and less than 5% secondary phases.
Suppressing segregated grain boundaries and enabling a continuous protective oxide will improve oxidation or corrosion resistance by two orders of magnitude.
Conventional sintering at 900–1000 °C for 2–4 hours gives less than 90% density, significant Mg volatilization, and coarse segregated microstructures.
CoCrFeNiTi mechanical-alloying/SPS results can be transferred to explain rapid densification of an Mg-transition-metal alloy.
Laves-phase formation in SPS-processed CrMoNbWV supports the proposed phase-avoidance threshold for the Mg alloy.
